card.thesis: Mortgage insurance on a small down payment could usually have ended years earlier through rising home values than through the legal paydown schedule, but only on request.
card.overturns: "You're stuck paying mortgage insurance until your balance falls far enough on schedule."

claim: The legal right to cancel private mortgage insurance is keyed to paying the balance down to 80% of the home's original value, with automatic termination at 78%. For a buyer putting 5% down on a 30-year fixed loan at the average rate of the purchase quarter, that schedule took a median 11.58 years across the 173 purchase quarters from 1975 to 2018. If the home simply tracked the national house price index, the loan would have reached 80% of the home's current value in a median of 3.0 years; even under a stricter seasoning rule common among loan investors (at least 2 years, 75% until year 5, 80% after), the median was 4.0 years, and appreciation beat the schedule by 3 years or more for 87.9% of purchase quarters. It failed for only 2.9% of quarters, the 2005-2007 buyers. Using current value requires the borrower to ask and usually to pay for an appraisal. This is history, not a forecast.

numbers.definition: Cohorts: each quarter q from 1975Q1 in USSTHPI (FHFA all-transactions house price index, quarterly, NSA; a date's quarter = its month mapped to Q1-Q4). Loan: 30-year fixed, 95 borrowed on a home worth 100 (5% down), rate = arithmetic mean of the weekly MORTGAGE30US values whose dates fall in quarter q; level payment P = 95*i/(1-(1+i)^-360), i = rate/1200; balance after month m: b_m = b_{m-1}*(1+i) - P. Schedule time = first month m with b_m <= 80 (80% of original value). Value time = first month m that is a multiple of 3 (m = 3k) with quarter index q+k inside the HPI data and b_m / (100*HPI[q+k]/HPI[q]) <= LIMIT; if never, the cohort is 'not reached'. Cohorts are kept only if the quarter index q + ceil(schedule months/3) is inside the HPI data (last quarter 2026Q2), which keeps 1975Q1-2018Q1 (173 cohorts). LIMIT = 0.80 at any month. provisions.cite: CFPB, "When can I remove private mortgage insurance (PMI) from my loan?" (borrower-requested cancellation, Homeowners Protection Act rules)
provisions.quote: You have the right to ask your servicer to cancel PMI on the date the principal balance of your mortgage is scheduled to fall to 80 percent of the original value of your home.
your servicer must automatically terminate PMI on the date when your principal balance is scheduled to reach 78 percent of the original value of your home.

provisions.cite: CFPB, same page (investor guidelines may be more favorable)
provisions.quote: Loan investors, including Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac, often create their own PMI cancellation guidelines. But these guidelines cannot be less favorable to the borrower than the ones above.

assumptions: The home's value moves exactly with the national all-transactions house price index; local markets vary widely.
Down payment 5%, 30-year fixed at the quarter's average survey rate, only scheduled payments, no refinancing.
The seasoning rule (2 years minimum, 75% before year 5, 80% after) stands in for loan-investor guidelines; actual servicer rules, appraisal requirements and payment-history conditions vary.
The schedule benchmark is the borrower-request date at 80% of original value; automatic termination at 78% comes later still.
limits: History, not a forecast. National averages hide local price declines; the 2005-2007 cohorts show appreciation can fail. Cancelling on current value depends on the loan investor's rules, an appraisal the borrower may have to pay for, and a written request; the right keyed to original value is the only one guaranteed for these loans.
